questions.q: What is the core principle behind segregation of duties?
options: Every user should have the maximum access possible to work efficiently
No single person should hold conflicting access that lets them both initiate and approve the same business event unsupervised
Only managers are allowed to use the system
Every transaction must be entered twice by two different systems
questions.explain: Segregation of duties exists to prevent one person from pushing through an improper transaction with no independent check, by ensuring conflicting duties aren't held by the same individual.

questions.q: Does Oracle Fusion automatically prevent a role from combining two conflicting duties, such as creating a supplier and approving its payments?
options: Yes, Oracle Fusion blocks any such role from ever being created
Only for General Ledger roles, never for Payables
Only if Advanced Access Controls is turned off
No — Oracle will provision a role combining both capabilities if an administrator builds and assigns it that way; SoD is a design discipline, not a built-in restriction
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion does not predefine or automatically enforce SoD business logic. Preventing conflicts is a role-design discipline applied by the implementation team.

questions.q: An SoD conflict is best described as existing at which level?
options: Across a person's combined access from all of their roles together
Within a single role in isolation, regardless of who holds it
Only within the Security Console's role hierarchy view
Only in abstract roles, never in job roles
questions.explain: An SoD conflict is about combined access: two individually reasonable roles can still create a conflict the moment the same person holds both.

questions.q: Which Oracle tool continuously monitors role assignments and transactions against a library of access-conflict rules in Oracle Fusion Cloud?
options: The Security Console's Manage Users task
Business Intelligence Publisher
Oracle Advanced Access Controls, part of Oracle Risk Management Cloud
Functional Setup Manager
questions.explain: Oracle Advanced Access Controls (within Oracle Risk Management Cloud) is the current tool for continuous SoD conflict monitoring and simulation in Fusion Cloud.

questions.q: Castellan Robotics' controller temporarily needs both invoice-approval and journal-posting access during a staffing gap, creating an unavoidable SoD conflict. What is the accepted response?
options: Ignore the conflict since it's temporary
Immediately terminate the controller's access to both functions
Disable segregation of duties monitoring company-wide
Document the conflict as an accepted risk and add a compensating control, such as a periodic independent review
questions.explain: When a conflict can't be immediately eliminated, best practice is to document it as an accepted risk and add a compensating control, such as a review by a second person, rather than ignoring it.
